# Results — Study 404 (Shooting Star) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — detect the
shooting-star geometry by exact OHLC rules, split by prior trend, trade the star **short**
(enter at the next close, hold 1/3/5/10 days), and measure the conditional short return
against each name's own **short base rate** — run across a fixed basket of **26 liquid US
large-caps + SPY** (full yfinance history, longest tape back to 1962). Inference: HAC
Newey–West one-sample t on the pooled edge + a per-name label-shuffle placebo. Prices are
**un-adjusted daily OHLC**; forward returns are **price-only** (no dividends). As-of
**2026-06-23** (latest complete bar). Basket content fingerprint **`d488237f4299`**.*

> **Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** The basket is names still trading in 2026.
> For a *bearish* claim this tilt cuts **against** the short (survivors are the names that
> kept rising), so a null/weak short edge is partly mechanical; a *positive* short edge
> would be the surprising one. Direction reasoned about explicitly, not buried.

## The honest test — shooting star (prior uptrend), traded SHORT, gross

The short edge = conditional short return minus the name's own short base rate (so each
name's drift is netted out). A real reversal would clear HAC *t* = **+2**.

| Horizon | n | cond (bps) | short base (bps) | **edge (bps)** | win-rate | **HAC *t*** | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day | 5,672 | −9.1 | −6.6 | **−3.1** | 45.3% | **−1.39** | 0.889 |
| 3 days | 5,668 | −21.9 | −19.6 | **−3.9** | 46.1% | **−0.97** | 0.816 |
| 5 days | 5,668 | −35.8 | −32.5 | **−6.1** | 45.2% | **−1.12** | 0.870 |
| 10 days | 5,666 | −58.0 | −64.0 | **+0.6** | 45.3% | **+0.07** | 0.465 |

- No horizon's short edge is positive-significant; the placebo *p*-values are all far above
  0.05 (random days clear this bar trivially). The win-rate is ~45% — *below* a coin.
- The conditional short return is strongly negative at every horizon — but so is the short
  base rate (shorting these rising names bleeds): the *edge* over the base rate is the honest
  number, and it sits at noise.

## "Calls the top?" — pool every star geometry, short it

Drop the trend label. If the long upper wick were bearish, this should at least lean positive.

| Horizon | n | edge (bps) | win-rate | **HAC *t*** | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day | 10,744 | **−3.9** | 45.2% | **−2.15** | 0.982 |
| 3 days | 10,740 | **−7.0** | 45.6% | **−2.23** | 0.987 |
| 5 days | 10,739 | **−8.7** | 45.4% | **−2.05** | 0.986 |

Shorting the star is **significantly negative** (HAC *t* ≈ −2.1 to −2.2). The long upper
wick, if it predicts anything, predicts **continuation up** — the exact opposite of the
"exhaustion / reversal" folklore. This is the myth-check stamp: **BUSTED**.

## Myth-check — does "only fade a star at the top of a strong rally" rescue it?

Keep only stars after a large trailing 10-day run-up (star, short, H=5):

| require trailing run-up of ≥ | n | edge (bps) | win-rate | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0% (no filter) | 5,668 | −6.1 | 45.2% | −1.12 |
| 5% | 1,759 | +3.8 | 46.5% | +0.35 |
| 10% | 477 | −6.2 | 47.6% | −0.23 |
| 15% | 143 | +0.8 | 47.6% | +0.02 |

The filter only thins the sample; the edge stays indistinguishable from zero. No rescue.

## Per-name breakdown (star, short, H=5)

Of **26** names, exactly **1** clears HAC *t* > 2 (PG, *t* = +2.38) — precisely what 26
independent draws produce by chance at the 5% level (the textbook multiple-testing
signature). The largest movers are *negative*: GS −93.1 bps (*t* = −1.50), INTC −74.3 bps
(*t* = −1.77). No coherent positive short edge across names.

## Cost sweep (star short, H=5; borrow 2 bps/day × 5 = 10 bps)

The star is a **short** — the most cost-laden side (spread twice + borrow per day). Starting
below zero, costs only deepen the loss:

| one-way cost | net edge (bps/event) |
|---|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross + borrow) | −16.1 |
| 1.0 bps | −18.1 |
| 5.0 bps | −26.1 |
| 10.0 bps | −36.1 |

There is no positive break-even cost — the gross is already negative.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's something to find

On a deterministic synthetic OHLC panel (`data.synthetic_panel`) the same engine recovers a
post-star decline **only when one is planted**, and reads ≈ 0 when it isn't (H = 1, the
planted horizon):

| Planted post-star decline | short edge (bps) | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| edge = 0 (random walk) | +0.1 | +0.03 | 0.49 |
| edge = 0.01 (real top) | +63.1 | +14.57 | 0.000 |

The harness catches a real top at *t* ≈ 15 and stays silent on noise — so the real-tape
`NONE` is a statement about the **market**, not the method.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Shooting-star short edge **−6.1 bps** at 5 days (HAC *t* = **−1.12**,
  placebo *p* = **0.87**); no horizon, filter, or name carries a positive short edge past
  +2 (the lone one that does is multiple testing). Win-rate ~45% (below a coin).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Gross edge ≤ 0, and the short pays spread **and** borrow; net at
  5 days ≈ **−26.1 bps/event**. No positive break-even cost exists.
- **Calls the top? — BUSTED.** Pooling every star, the short edge is **−3.9 bps** at HAC
  *t* = **−2.15** (significant, wrong sign): the long upper wick leans toward continuation
  up. On modern US large-caps the shooting star does not mark the top.
